item.title: Former UN envoy says Iran war was 'perfectly avoidable'
item.description:
Former UN envoy says Iran war was 'perfectly avoidable'

Iran war could have been avoided, Álvaro de Soto, a former UN special coordinator for the Middle East peace process, has said.

“It was perfectly avoidable. It need not have happened,” he said, adding that US officials have offered differing explanations for going to war.

Speaking at MED Dialogues conference in Naples, he said: “Lasting peace requires a willingness to confront the problems at the root of a conflict. Without addressing them, opportunities for peace will continue to be missed.”

item.title: Turkish foreign minister says Iran war fallout threatening global markets
item.description:
Turkish foreign minister says Iran war fallout threatening global markets

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan has said the economic burden brought by the US-Israel war is getting harder for many countries, while emphasising a ceasefire was needed to reverse global financial crises.

Speaking to Turkish broadcaster TGRT Haber on Saturday, Fidan warned that the fallout from the conflict is threatening international markets.

“It is heading toward having very destructive effects,” he said.

Fidan said diplomatic efforts to re-open the Strait of Hormuz remain active, even though the process appears to be deadlocked, citing his recent discussion with Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani.

He also said that Ankara was keeping the humanitarian crisis in Gaza on the global radar permanently despite other international crises.

"In every speech, every initiative, and every platform wherever it may be, the Gaza issue is one we have not, and will not, allow to be forgotten," Fidan said.

item.title: Israeli occupation, Iranian interference threat to Lebanese sovereignty, Aoun says
item.description:
Israeli occupation, Iranian interference threat to Lebanese sovereignty, Aoun says

Lebanese President Joseph Aoun has accused Iran of meddling in Lebanon's affairs through Hezbollah's weapons and also demanded Israel withdraw from the country's south.

In a speech on the eve of Lebanon's 83rd independence anniversary, Aoun vowed to press ahead with plans to bring all weapons under state control. 

Lebanon's sovereignty still faces two threats, he said: "The Israeli occupation of parts of our territory" and foreign interference from "influential elements within the Iranian regime" through weapons and decisions outside the authority of the Lebanese state. 

On Israel, Aoun stressed Lebanon's message was clear and direct: "Withdraw from every inch of Lebanese territory. Stop your attacks."

There would be "no occupation ever again", he said. "And no weapons outside the state that... serve the interests of, foreign powers," he added, without naming a specific group.

Such weapons may once have served a purpose, he said, but later imposed a high cost on Lebanon when they came to serve causes beyond its borders. 

"You must hand over your weapons," Aoun said.

The Lebanese government has committed to disarming Hezbollah, whose arsenal has long outstripped that of the national army and which has justified its weapons as necessary to resist Israel.

In June, Lebanon and Israel signed a framework agreement that included the disarmament of Hezbollah, a gradual Israeli withdrawal from territories it occupies in the south and the deployment of the Lebanese army to the area.

But implementation has stalled and Hezbollah has refused to surrender its weapons.

Israel's army still carries out strikes, shelling and detonations in the south, where its forces are operating in a self-declared "security zone" running around 10 kilometres.

Report by AFP

item.title: Pezeshkian says Iran engaged in 'silent economic war' as blockade completes 130 days
item.description:
Pezeshkian says Iran engaged in 'silent economic war' as blockade completes 130 days

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has said that his country was engaged in a "silent war that is far more difficult than the one in which missiles are launched and destruction is inflicted".

In a video shared by Al Jazeera, Pezeshkian said: "It is an economic war, one that you, as those working on the economic front, are dealing with. It is by no means an easy one." 

While the Iranian economy has been under duress for years in the face of international sanctions, this year’s US naval blockade on Iranian oil and new sanctions imposed since the start of the war have increased the pressure manifold. 

Kazem Gharibabadi, Iran’s Deputy Foreign Minister for Legal and International Affairs, on Saturday described the naval blockade an act of war, vowing that the country would take action to break it, according to Mehr news agency.

On Saturday, the US Central Command said "today marks 130 consecutive days of America's blockade against Iran".

"US service members are enforcing the blockade with exceptional focus, determination, and professionalism — preventing Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps from exporting billions of dollars in crude oil," Centcom said on X.

item.title: Suffolk village votes to ‘leave the UK’ over plans to house asylum seekers nearby
item.description:
Local MP says legitimate criticisms of asylum housing plans are being co-opted by opposition parties ‘stirring up racial discord’

Residents of a Suffolk village have voted to “leave the UK” in a referendum held in response to government plans to house 930 asylum seekers at a nearby former military base.

Approximately 500 people in Barnham were eligible to take part in the symbolic vote on Saturday. There were 257 votes for independence, 16 against and one spoiled ballot.

item.title: Trump threatens ‘tremendous penalties’ for US tech firms that build datacenters abroad
item.description:
President gives wide-ranging White House press conference and says he has ‘fantastic relationships’ with Putin and Xi

Donald Trump threatened on Friday to impose “tremendous penalties” on American tech companies that build datacenters outside the US, though he gave no details and told reporters he had not yet informed his own officials about the plan.

In a discursive press conference from the White House briefing room, Trump also said he would “look into” the report that Iran had been planning to possibly detonate a “dirty bomb” in Washington DC, and backed JD Vance over comments the vice-president made blaming Republican midterm losses on the Iran war.
